name: SKMR4
notes: Drawn for MX Shooting Calculator from the published subtension figures in https://verwaltung.kahles.at/files/shares/Absehen/Dokumente/2026_all_FW/SKMR4_K318i_K525i.PDF; the layout was read from the picture, not traced. Kahles drawing SKMR4 for K318i/K525i (02023011293-106, 11.03.2020); first focal plane, so the mrad values hold at every magnification. PUBLISHED and used (page 2, dimensioned view): crosshair line width 0.035 mil and centre dot 0.035 mil diameter; 16 mil between the inner ends of the horizontal posts (posts from +-8) and 8 mil from the horizontal line to the top post; post thickness 0.3 mil; 0.5 mil marks on the posts; 1 mil hash spacing with 0.2 mil subdivisions; 1-mil marks 0.5 mil and half-mil marks 0.25 mil long on the vertical stadia; subdivision marks 0.07 mil long; detail A: 0.2 and 0.5 mil marks on the lower stadia, tree rows every 1 mil below centre with 0.15 mil whole-mil windage marks and 0.1 mil half-mil windage marks (labels 2..12; which call-out belongs to which mark is our reading of the arrows). ESTIMATED from the picture (page 1, measured at about 136 px per mil): tree row k is k/2 mil wide each side (rows 1-14 complete), its windage marks every 0.5 mil out to k/2-0.5 (whole-mil marks cross the row, half-mil marks hang below); the 0.2-mil subdivision marks sit one-sided, 0.2 and 0.8 below the horizontal line / right of the vertical line and 0.4 and 0.6 on the other side; an extra 0.1-mil fine scale between 3 and 4 mil on all four arms (0.1/0.9 on the 0.4 side, 0.3/0.7 on the 0.2 side, 3.5 mark 0.25 mil long); no half-mil marks on the horizontal line apart from 3.5; the 1-mil marks on the horizontal line 0.5 mil long; open centre with the lines starting 0.15 mil from the aim point; post marks every 1 mil from 8 to 15 mil, 0.035 mil stroke; tree rows and marks drawn 0.035 mil wide like the crosshair. Tree rows 1-14 are drawn; row 15 is cut off by the drawing's field circle (radius about 15.75 mil), so its width is not known and it is left out. The lower stadia visibly continue to that circle, so they are drawn to 15.75 mil with their marks (0.2, 0.4, 0.5, 0.6 below 15). Post marks beyond 15 mil are not shown. Posts and their marks are black; everything else is red (illuminated). Numerals not drawn.

notes: Drawn for MX Shooting Calculator from the published subtension figures in https://assets.ctfassets.net/pvkenuwtinkd/7Ix4xOu19oTw8ePRChuC9w/e3072387e960acfcd65d765b707931da/BRW_BRW-I_180x270_EN_Druck.pdf; the layout was read from the picture, not traced. PUBLISHED and used (MOA, Z5(i)+ 2-10x42 BT, 3.5-18x50 P BT and 5-25x56 P BT alike): A 2 = centre to the first hold-over dot, 2 MOA between hold overs; B 1 = length of the windage marks on the hold-over lines; C 2 = their spacing; D 22 = centre to the bottom heavy post; E 42 = gap between the horizontal heavy posts; F 1 = spacing of the windage marks on the main crosshair (1 to 20 MOA each side); G 5 = centre to the first long mark (long marks at 5, 10, 15, 20); H 0.70 = short main-crosshair mark length; I 1.50 = long mark length (marks centred on the line); J 0.29 = centre dot; K 0.15 = thin line width; L 0.88 = heavy post thickness; M 0.50 = hold-over dots. Reading of the ladder: the hold-over dots and the hold-over lines alternate and every one of them is a hold over 2 MOA from the next (dots at 2, 6, 10, 14, 18 MOA, lines at 4, 8, 12, 16, 20 MOA below the centre). This follows the BRW sheet, whose drawing is to scale (its 1 MOA main-crosshair marks and E fit) and whose A runs from the crosshair to the first dot, and Swarovski's BRS and BRW icons, which show the same ladder at the same scale; the BRS sheet places A on the first line and stretches its ladder sideways, which is taken as a drafting simplification. Line n carries n windage marks each side (every 2 MOA) and runs one step past them (half widths 4, 6, 8, 10, 12 MOA); the marks hang below the line. ESTIMATED from the picture: the top post starts at 22 MOA like the bottom one; posts run to the field edge. Second focal plane: the values hold at each scope's highest magnification only ("The shown values only apply to the highest magnification of the scope"), so published_at_magnification is null; the same values are published for all three scopes. Illumination: only the centre point lights (BRW-I). Same ladder as BRS (non-BT models).

name: #60 (V8 1.1-8x24)
notes: Drawn for MX Shooting Calculator from the published subtension figures in https://www.zeiss.com/content/dam/pno/downloads/riflescopes/datasheets/datasheet-illuminated-reticle-60.pdf (and the 2026 US catalog, https://www.zeiss.com/content/dam/pno/downloads/_local/united-states/catalog-zeiss-hunting-shooting-us.pdf, p. 44-45); the layout was read from the picture, not traced. PUBLISHED and used (cm at 100 m at 8x, the data sheet's ZEISS V8 8x column): A 1.3 = fine line thickness; B 5.4 = heavy post thickness; C 0.8 = illuminated dot diameter (footnote: 6.6 cm / magnification for V8, HT and V6, 7.1 cm / magnification for V4); D 175 = bar opening, post tip to post tip. Catalog (as "V8 1.1-8x30") @8x: A 0.5, B 2.1, C 0.3, D 34 MOA. Opening: the data sheet's labelled drawing puts D across the whole gap from the left post tip to the right post tip, and the large drawing on its page 3 shows that gap as 34 % of the field circle, which fits D against the field of view (e.g. 175 cm in the 5.4 m field of the V8 1.1-8x24 at 8x = 32 %; 350 cm in 9.5 m for the V4 1-4x24 at 4x = 37 %). The 2026 US catalog draws its "Opening" from the centre to the post tip and prints about half the data-sheet value; its picture, too, shows a gap of about a third of the field, so the catalog number is the centre-to-post half. The data sheet wins: D is post tip to post tip, so the side posts start at D/2 left and right of the centre. ESTIMATED from the picture: there is no top post (the fine line runs to the edge of the field); the bottom post starts D/2 below the centre, the same distance as the side posts (drawing: 648 px against 646 px); the posts run to the field edge; the fine crosshair has width A between the posts; only the centre dot lights up. As published, the dot (C) is smaller than the line thickness (A), so it shows as a red point on the crossing. Second focal plane: the figures hold at 8x and scale with 1/magnification (data sheet tables 1.1x to 35x). Successor of reticle 40. Data sheet dated 10/2021; catalog pages 44-45.

name: #54 (V8 1.8-14x50)
notes: Drawn for MX Shooting Calculator from the published subtension figures in https://www.zeiss.com/content/dam/pno/downloads/riflescopes/datasheets/datasheet-illuminated-reticle-54.pdf; the layout was read from the picture, not traced. PUBLISHED: nothing for this scope. The data sheet marks #54 "Not available" for the V8 1.8-14x50, but the V8 product page lists "54 | 60" for it, so it is drawn. ESTIMATED: THE ANGULAR SIZE IS AN ESTIMATE. The drawing is taken to be the same as on the V8 1.1-8x24 and its size is scaled from the V8 1.1-8x24 table's 1/magnification law (A about 14.4 cm, B about 220 cm, C = 6.6 cm, each divided by the magnification), giving at 14x A 1.03 = line thickness, B 15.7 = full height of the vertical line, C 0.47 = illuminated dot diameter. That assumes the 1.8-14x50 uses the same reticle size per magnification as the 1.1-8x24, which #60 does across the V8 line. Layout as on the 1.1-8x24: vertical line centred on the crossing, both lines width A, horizontal line to the field edge, only the dot lights up. Second focal plane: the estimate is for 14x and scales with 1/magnification. Evolution of reticle 0. This copy is rescaled from 14x to 13.5x (14/13.5), the reference magnification of the scopes using it.

name: #60 (V8 1.8-14x50)
notes: Drawn for MX Shooting Calculator from the published subtension figures in https://www.zeiss.com/content/dam/pno/downloads/riflescopes/datasheets/datasheet-illuminated-reticle-60.pdf (and the 2026 US catalog, https://www.zeiss.com/content/dam/pno/downloads/_local/united-states/catalog-zeiss-hunting-shooting-us.pdf, p. 44-45); the layout was read from the picture, not traced. PUBLISHED and used (cm at 100 m at 14x, the data sheet's ZEISS V8 14x column): A 0.7 = fine line thickness; B 3.1 = heavy post thickness; C 0.5 = illuminated dot diameter (footnote: 6.6 cm / magnification for V8, HT and V6, 7.1 cm / magnification for V4); D 100 = bar opening, post tip to post tip. Catalog @14x: A 0.3, B 1.2, C 0.2, D 19.5 MOA. The figures hold at 14x as printed; the scope tops out at 13.5x. Opening: the data sheet's labelled drawing puts D across the whole gap from the left post tip to the right post tip, and the large drawing on its page 3 shows that gap as 34 % of the field circle, which fits D against the field of view (e.g. 175 cm in the 5.4 m field of the V8 1.1-8x24 at 8x = 32 %; 350 cm in 9.5 m for the V4 1-4x24 at 4x = 37 %). The 2026 US catalog draws its "Opening" from the centre to the post tip and prints about half the data-sheet value; its picture, too, shows a gap of about a third of the field, so the catalog number is the centre-to-post half. The data sheet wins: D is post tip to post tip, so the side posts start at D/2 left and right of the centre. ESTIMATED from the picture: there is no top post (the fine line runs to the edge of the field); the bottom post starts D/2 below the centre, the same distance as the side posts (drawing: 648 px against 646 px); the posts run to the field edge; the fine crosshair has width A between the posts; only the centre dot lights up. As published, the dot (C) is smaller than the line thickness (A), so it shows as a red point on the crossing. Second focal plane: the figures hold at 14x and scale with 1/magnification (data sheet tables 1.1x to 35x). Successor of reticle 40. Data sheet dated 10/2021; catalog pages 44-45. This copy is rescaled from 14x to 13.5x (14/13.5), the reference magnification of the scopes using it.

name: #43 (V8 4.8-35x60)
notes: Drawn for MX Shooting Calculator from the published subtension figures in https://www.zeiss.com/content/dam/pno/downloads/riflescopes/datasheets/datasheet-illuminated-reticle-43.pdf (and https://www.zeiss.com/content/dam/pno/downloads/riflescopes/datasheets/datasheet-non-illuminated-reticle-43.pdf); the layout was read from the picture, not traced. PUBLISHED and used (cm at 100 m at 30x, data sheet 30x columns): A 0.3 = fine line thickness; B 1.7 = heavy post thickness; C 1.3 = black dot diameter; D 0.2 = illuminated centre dot diameter (footnote: 6.6 cm / magnification); E 10 = dot spacing (= 1 mrad at 30x); F 100 = bar opening. The V8 4.8-35x60 and Conquest V6 5-30x50 tables are identical from 6x to 30x, so one entry serves both; the figures hold at 30x (not at the V8 4.8-35x60's 35x, where #43 is A 0.3, B 1.4, C 1.1, D 0.2, E 9, F 86). The non-illuminated #43 (Conquest V6 5-30x50, separate data sheet) has the same A, B, C, E and F and no D; its drawing shows a black centre dot of unpublished size where the red dot is, which this shared entry draws as the red D dot. Opening: F is post tip to post tip. The labelled drawing spans F across the whole gap, the table gives F = 10 E at every magnification, and the pictures place the post tips where a fifth dot would be (5 E from the centre); so the posts start at F/2 = 5 E. The catalog has no #43 table. ESTIMATED from the picture: four heavy posts (left, right, top and bottom; the large drawings on page 3 of both data sheets show a top post, so the research note's "no top post" is not followed); 4 black dots on each arm at 1-4 E, on the fine line, which runs only between the posts; the posts run to the field edge; only the centre dot lights up. The drawings put the first dot a little closer to the centre than E (about 0.75 E) but the outer dots and the post tips on whole E steps; the published even spacing E is used. The drawings are not to scale against the field (F is about 73 % of the field of view by the published figures, 25 % in the drawing) and draw the red dot larger than the black dots although the table makes it much smaller (D is even smaller than the line thickness A, so it shows as a red point on the crossing); the published figures are used. Second focal plane: the figures hold at the stated magnification and scale with 1/magnification. Data sheets dated 10/2021.
